item.title: [NVDA Bullish (+0.49)] Jim Cramer Breaks Down P/E Multiples Explaining Why NVIDIA (NVDA) Looks Cheaper Than ServiceNow
item.description:
Sentiment: NVDA Bullish (+0.49)
Jim Cramer highlighted on Mad Money that despite its higher nominal share price, NVIDIA (NVDA) is cheaper than ServiceNow (NOW) when considering their P/E multiples, both current and forward-looking. He explained that NVIDIA's lower P/E ratio, despite its phenomenal growth, is attributed by some to beliefs that its numbers are peaking or a pause in data center spending due to political opposition. Cramer vehemently disagreed with these criticisms, emphasizing the importance of P/E multiples over nominal stock prices for valuation.

item.title: [MSFT Bullish (+0.23), NVDA Bullish (+0.44), AMZN Bullish (+0.26)] Equinix turns the network into the control plane for enterprise AI inference

item.title: [AMZN Neutral (-0.10)] Federal Regulators Open Investigation After Tesla Launches Car With No Steering Wheel
item.description:
Sentiment: AMZN Neutral (-0.10)
Federal regulators have opened an audit into Tesla's Cybercab, a new passenger vehicle launched without a steering wheel or pedals, after Tesla self-certified it as street-legal rather than going through the standard federal exemption process. This move bypasses the lengthy Part 555 exemption process typically required for vehicles not meeting all safety standards, a path previously taken by Zoox which took years. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is examining Tesla's certification process and technical data, especially how the company determined certain federal motor vehicle safety standards were inapplicable to the Cybercab.
